clue.text: Nice gaff — wants one, having no accommodation?

indicators.note: having no accommodation means there is no room for the one, so it is left out of the word

parts.note: to want something is to desire it, so wants gives desires
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone homeless longs for a fine house of their own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gaff' is British slang for a home; DES RES is estate-agent shorthand for a desirable residence.
explanation.definitionFit: Estate-agent slang for a desirable residence, a smart house, which 'nice gaff' says in street slang.

clue.text: Girl in farce, 'The Ladykillers'

indicators.note: in signals that the name sits inside the run of letters across the words farce and The Ladykillers

explanation.surface: A young woman appears in a stage comedy of the famous Ealing film.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional female first name, so an example of a girl's name.

clue.text: Momentary mental aberration, losing head in squall

indicators.note: losing head tells us to drop the opening letter of the word for the aberration

parts.note: a brainstorm is a sudden fit of mental confusion

explanation.surface: Someone has a brief lapse of reason while caught out in a gale.
explanation.definitionFit: A squall is a sudden violent gust with rain, a kind of storm.

clue.text: Saying by Fahrenheit Italian deemed appropriate

parts.note: a saw is an old saying or proverb
IT is the usual abbreviation for Italian, as in Italian vermouth

explanation.surface: A proverb about temperature is judged suitable by an Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: To see fit is an idiom for judging something proper, so in the past tense it means considered suitable.

clue.text: Emperor's East European origins initially concealed by grandma

indicators.note: concealed by means the other pieces are hidden within the word for grandma

parts.note: nan is a familiar name for a grandmother
a Pole comes from Poland in eastern Europe

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word origins

explanation.surface: An emperor's roots in eastern Europe were kept secret by his grandmother.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonaparte crowned himself Emperor of the French in 1804.

clue.text: Criminal misusing ATM loot as collector of bits and pieces?

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are treated in a crooked way, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A crook abuses a cash machine and hoards the stolen money.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: 'bits' and 'pieces' are both words for coins, which a coin collector gathers.
explanation.definitionFit: A coin collector collects pieces of money, here jokingly called bits and pieces.

clue.text: Contagious fear across Mediterranean over swine flu, for example

indicators.note: across means the word for fear stretches over the other piece, holding it

parts.note: panic is a fear that spreads through a crowd

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the abbreviation is turned upside down, read backwards

explanation.surface: Fear of infection spreads across the Mediterranean because of swine flu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contagious fear' looks like the definition but is the container; the definition is the example at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Swine flu in 2009 spread worldwide, making it an example of a worldwide outbreak of disease.

clue.text: Spikes — they may be used in running shoes

definitions.meaning: to spike or lace a drink is to add alcohol to it secretly

definitions.text: they may be used in running shoes
definitions.meaning: strings that tie up a pair of trainers

explanation.surface: Athletes' spiked shoes are tied with these strings.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiking a drink is lacing it, and strings tie running shoes, so both senses fit the word.

clue.text: Film paid for by municipality?

definitions.meaning: a 1949 musical starring Gene Kelly and Frank Sinatra
charged to the town council, at the town's expense

explanation.surface: A movie whose costs are met by the local council.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means out enjoying the nightlife, and is also the title of a classic Hollywood musical film.

clue.text: Female executive — I should be employed by daily

indicators.note: being employed by the cleaner here means sitting within her name

parts.note: a daily is a British term for a cleaning woman who comes in each day, a charwoman

explanation.surface: A businesswoman wonders whether she should hire a cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: The woman who presides over a board or committee, a senior figure in charge.

clue.text: Clever suggestion saving time

indicators.note: saving means keeping something within, so the word for suggestion holds the other letter

parts.note: a cue is a hint or prompt

explanation.surface: A smart idea that saves time.
explanation.definitionFit: In American and older usage, the word means shrewd or sharp-witted.

clue.text: Course for important horse races

definitions.meaning: a course of study of ancient Greek and Latin
the five chief British flat races, such as the Derby

explanation.surface: A racecourse hosts the season's major meetings.
explanation.definitionFit: A university course in ancient Greek and Roman culture, and the name for Britain's five top flat races.

clue.text: Dressed trees round area for festival

indicators.note: round means the rearranged letters go around the area's letter
dressed means arranged or set out, so the letters of the trees are rearranged

explanation.surface: Decorated trees set around a square for a spring celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressed' rearranges TREES to ESTER, which goes round A.
explanation.definitionFit: The Christian feast of the Resurrection is a religious festival held each spring.

clue.text: Circles round small lake in capital

indicators.note: round means the two rings go around the other letters

parts.note: two circles look like two letter Os

explanation.surface: Rowers circle a little lake in a city.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Norway, so an example of a capital.

clue.text: Silly old prunes getting something special

indicators.note: silly suggests the letters behave foolishly and get jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Some foolish old dried plums are getting something special.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnificence or grandeur, something special and impressive to see.

clue.text: Advanced through jostling into flight

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for advanced, as in A level
via means by way of, through

indicators.note: jostling means the letters are pushed about, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone pushed forward through a jostling crowd to get onto a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: The practice of flying aircraft, so flight in the general sense.

clue.text: Pull in heavy drinker of the highest social standing

indicators.note: in means the word for pull goes inside the drinker

parts.note: a toper is a habitual drunkard
to draw is to pull

explanation.surface: A pub draws in a hard drinker from high society.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for the very best or most upper-class, like the top drawer of a chest holding the finest things.

clue.text: Relatives, American, in the US government

parts.note: uncles are family relatives

explanation.surface: Family members from America are working in Washington.
explanation.definitionFit: The cartoon figure in a top hat personifies the federal government of America.

clue.text: Aquatic bird, brilliantly red duck

parts.note: flaming describes a vivid red like fire
a duck in cricket is a score of zero, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A water bird and a bright red duck.
explanation.definitionFit: A pink wading bird living around shallow lakes and lagoons.

clue.text: See this conifer in film studio, not wood

indicators.note: not means the word wood is removed from the studio's name

parts.note: Pinewood Studios is a famous film studio near London

explanation.surface: Spot this evergreen tree at a film studio, but not in a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: Pinewood Studios, west of London, is where many Bond films were made.
explanation.definitionFit: The pine is a common evergreen cone-bearing tree.

clue.text: Firmly established dock for the bay?

definitions.meaning: steady and secure, not likely to give way
a bay is a reddish-brown horse, and a stall is where it is housed

explanation.surface: A secure berth for a bay horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Steady and secure, and also a building where horses such as a bay are kept.

clue.text: Declare invalid must check blood group yearly

indicators.note: to check is to hold in, so the word for declaring invalid holds the blood group

parts.note: to annul is to declare void
A is one of the human blood groups

explanation.surface: Someone cancels something because a blood test must be done.
explanation.definitionFit: Happening once every year, so occurring on a yearly basis.

clue.text: Situated in a city, elegant for the most part

indicators.note: for the most part means taking nearly all of the word, losing its final letter

parts.note: urbane means suave and polished

explanation.surface: A city dweller is mostly sophisticated.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to a town or city, as opposed to rural.

clue.text: According to plan, got rent reviewed around middle of May

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters go about the central letter
reviewed suggests looking again and changing the order of the letters
middle of picks the central letter of May

explanation.surface: A landlord collected the rent and checked it in mid-May as planned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reviewed' rearranges GOT RENT to ONTRGET, which goes around A.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for being on course to meet a goal, so going as planned.

clue.text: Set up vote for Right to oust Left

indicators.note: to oust means one letter replaces the other, driving it out

parts.note: to elect is to vote in

explanation.surface: A political call for voters to back the right and throw out the left.
explanation.definitionFit: To erect a structure is to build it or raise it up.

clue.text: Male cat, black, in vault

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A black tomcat lurks in a crypt.
explanation.definitionFit: A burial vault, a chamber for the dead.

clue.text: Cricketer, lbw, is prone to come a cropper

indicators.note: to come a cropper is to fall badly, so the letters tumble into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A batsman given out leg before wicket is likely to fail.
explanation.walkthrough: LBW is leg before wicket, a way of getting out in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowler who makes the ball turn off the pitch, a type of cricketer.

clue.text: Male in carriage is forward

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation for male goes inside the other word

parts.note: transit is the conveyance or carriage of goods

explanation.surface: A man in a coach is pushy.
explanation.definitionFit: To forward something is to send it on, pass it along.

clue.text: Rotten type, in time, will cause mistakes in print

indicators.note: in means the rotten type sits inside the word for time

parts.note: an era is a period of time
a rat is a nasty, treacherous person

explanation.surface: A bad typeface, in time, will produce printing errors.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of corrections to errors in a printed book.
